input: B2B customer support product using Telegram as the backend. Original idea: 12 bots, 12 conversations per agent, route requests to free bot slots. Minimal POC. Asked about existing market solutions.
codebaseAnalysis: Hotline HQ repo scanned for conventions only (product is a separate repo): Telegram usage today is outbound-only raw HTTPS in service/notifier.js; bot tokens stored in notification_channels SQLite table; room_requests is a queue/status template; SSE infra mature; whatsapp.js session-Map is the poller template; long-polling preferred over webhooks for POC.

marketResearch.verdict: Crowded at bottom, empty at top; forum-topics pattern validated but no polished English-first SaaS; risks: low price anchors, weak US Telegram penetration

qa.a: Separate repo, standalone sellable product; Hotline HQ is tenant #1 / POC testbed

qa.q: 12-bot pool vs one bot + forum topics vs DM routing?
qa.a: One bot + forum topics (accepted pushback: bots have no concurrency limit, can't DM first)

qa.q: How do customers start a conversation?
qa.a: Web chat widget bridging to Telegram (US dealers don't use Telegram)

qa.q: How do conversations get an owner?
qa.a: Hybrid: round-robin @mention suggestion, any agent can answer

qa.q: What can agents do beyond reply?
qa.a: /close, /note, pinned customer info card; canned replies skipped
Live pilot on hotlinehq.online with real dealer traffic, 2-4 weeks
Auto-purge after 90 days, DB + Telegram topics
Supportgram / supportgram.io (owner preference; Claude recommended GramSupport whose .com was free)

securityNonNegotiables: rate limiting on public widget endpoints
acceptedRisks: Telegram cloud is a data processor for all customer content (inherent to product)
weak US Telegram penetration among support teams
